result.summary:
Checked out and confirmed feature/WF02-REQ369-20260917, HEAD 2cf84a99. Read handoffs/WF02-REQ369-20260917/step-05-release-validation.json (RELEASE-VALIDATOR's PASS-WITH-PENDING routing me here for AC6/AC7).

Read README.md's 'QA deployment' section: https://qa.bizdala.com is a real live instance, deploy infra in the sibling ai-dala-infra repo, credentials fetched via ai-dala-infra/scripts/qa-login.sh <username> (admin-user = PLATFORM_ADMIN, per the seeded-user table).

Before attempting login, checked whether QA can even reflect this branch's changes. docs/requirements.yaml's CD-deploy requirement (the section covering cd.yml, around line ~26740-26762) documents that QA deploys are triggered by CI on merge to main via a path-filter gate reusing ci.yml's changes job -- i.e. QA only ever reflects what has actually merged to main, never an open feature branch. Confirmed the actual git state: `git log main -1` and `git log origin/main -1` both show 43a39fa5 as the tip of main; this branch's own commits (259fd95a PlatformDashboardPage + routing, 84200c52, b19f122d, 2cf84a99) sit on top of that and are unmerged.

Verified this empirically against the live instance rather than trusting the inference alone: fetched https://qa.bizdala.com/ (200, real Letflow SPA shell), extracted its served bundle path (/assets/index-Bm3IRknt.js), downloaded it (357121 bytes), and grepped it for the two strings this requirement's own code introduces: `platform-dashboard` (0 matches) and `Platform Overview` (0 matches). Neither the new route nor the new page's fixed heading exists anywhere in the bundle QA is actually serving. (Requesting https://qa.bizdala.com/platform-dashboard directly returns HTTP 200, but that is only the SPA's catch-all index.html fallback for client-side routing -- not evidence the route is registered; the bundle-content check above is the real evidence and it is negative.)

This matches this task's own predicted-blocker framing and REQ-360's own precedent precisely in the opposite direction: REQ-360's scenario was authored against routing behaviour that ALREADY existed on main/QA at the time (no code change was required for that requirement -- it documented existing behaviour), so its live-QA run never depended on an unmerged branch going out first. REQ-369 is different in kind: it ships new frontend code (PlatformDashboardPage.tsx, router.tsx's new route, OidcCallbackPage.tsx's role-conditional redirect) that has no path to QA except through a merge to main and a subsequent CD deploy. There is no existing precedent in this repo for running live-QA UAT against an unmerged feature branch's not-yet-deployed code, and no mechanism (e.g. an ephemeral per-branch preview environment) exists to make that possible -- deploy is main-triggered only.

Did not attempt to fetch credentials or drive a login, since there is nothing on QA yet for a PLATFORM_ADMIN login to actually land on -- doing so would at best reproduce the pre-REQ-369 behaviour (redirect to shared / root, ISS-0700's known gap) and recording that as if it were this requirement's AC6/AC7 evidence would be exactly the fabrication this role is forbidden from doing.

CONCLUSION: AC6 and AC7 cannot be genuinely satisfied right now. This is not a defect in FRONTEND-DEV's implementation, RELEASE-VALIDATOR's Step 5 pass, or in the scenario-fixture update -- all of that is real and independently verified per step-05's report. It is a sequencing fact: live-QA verification of new frontend code structurally cannot happen before that code reaches QA, and QA only receives code via a merge-triggered CD deploy.
